title: Daily Market Digest
subtitle: Summary for Friday, August 21, 2026 (Markets Closed Sunday, August 23, 2026)

sections.title: Market Pulse: US Stocks Rebound to Close Volatile Week

items.headline: U.S. Equities End Week on Positive Note Despite Jumpy Bond Market
items.summary: U.S. stocks concluded a volatile week with gains on Friday, trimming earlier losses, even as the bond market remained under pressure. Hopes for robust corporate profits were boosted by an S&P Global report indicating U.S. business activity reached a 52-month high. Artificial intelligence continued to be a significant driver of earnings growth, with the S&P 500's second-quarter EPS growing 40.6% year-over-year.

items.headline: SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc. surged
items.summary: SELLAS Life Sciences Group Inc. ($SLS) saw a significant increase of 15.37%, closing at $15.46.

items.headline: Robinhood Markets jumped
items.summary: Robinhood Markets ($HOOD) climbed 13.7% amid increasing hopes for favorable crypto industry legislation in Washington.

items.headline: Coinbase Global gained
items.summary: Coinbase Global ($COIN) advanced 8.2% on optimistic sentiment surrounding potential crypto regulations.

items.headline: Freeport-McMoRan rose
items.summary: Freeport-McMoRan ($FCX) saw a 7.6% increase as gold prices continued their ascent.

items.headline: Ross Stores rallied after strong earnings
items.summary: Ross Stores ($ROST) rallied 4.4% following a stronger-than-expected profit and revenue report for its latest quarter.

items.headline: Boston Beer sank on CFO departure news
items.summary: Boston Beer ($SAM) declined 2.6% after the company announced the departure of its chief financial officer.

items.headline: Healthcare and Energy Led Weekly Sector Performance
items.summary: For the week ending August 21, the healthcare sector was the top performer, rising 4.19%, followed by energy, which gained 2.39%. Conversely, industrials and utilities were the weakest sectors, declining 4.23% and 3.65% respectively.

items.headline: U.S. Business Activity Reaches 52-Month High
items.summary: A preliminary report from S&P Global indicated that U.S. business activity expanded to a 52-month high, fueling optimism for corporate profit growth.

items.headline: Treasury Interventions and Yields
items.summary: The U.S. Treasury Department boosted its long-term debt buyback plans, with Secretary Scott Bessent announcing a doubling of operations from $2 billion to at least $4 billion. Despite this, the yield on the 10-year Treasury note continued its climb, rising to 4.73% from 4.69% on Thursday.

items.headline: Commodities and Crypto See Gains
items.summary: Oil prices advanced, and gold prices surged, briefly exceeding $4,690 per ounce. Bitcoin also experienced a significant rally, climbing above $77,000, driven by hopes for supportive crypto legislation.

items.headline: Week Ahead: Jackson Hole Symposium and Nvidia Earnings Eyed
items.summary: The upcoming week will feature the Jackson Hole Economic Policy Symposium, with Federal Reserve Chairman Warsh expected to deliver a keynote speech. Major earnings reports, including Nvidia, will also be closely watched for insights into AI demand and broader market trends. Key economic data releases include the Personal Income and Outlays report for July and annual revisions to nonfarm payrolls.
